title: tastewatch digest: 2026-06-28
description:
tastewatch weekly taste digest — 2026-06-28 (window 2026-06-21 → 06-28, 72 non-merge commits). Prior digest: warren-307d (2026-06-14).

## 1. Verdict table (stratified sample, n=10)

| sha | subject (trunc) | verdict | article |
|-----|-----------------|---------|---------|
| 63739975 | #419 schema: nullable runs.target_branch + migration (#507) | conforms | I |
| 78881f65 | Enable RLS on conversations + messages (#463) | conforms | I/III |
| 1515380b | closed-loop alert healer: POST /alerts/heal | conforms | IV |
| 23470206 | Human-readable plan-run renderer (port jq → TS) (#456) | conforms | IV |
| 0dc4c979 | #487 plan-run: ready→active Plot promotion seam (#503) | conforms | I |
| 85e5cd3d | reap teardown: destroy burrow workspace on lost reconcile (#465) | conforms | I |
| bde49d91 | Release v0.9.8 (#517) | conforms | III |
| 3e5c40a2 | release v0.9.7 | conforms | III |
| 44123b3e | Decompose src/diagnostics/checks.ts (#461) | diverges | II |
| 1466ae81 | Refactor in-flight.ts under cog-complexity 15 (#475) | diverges | I |

Sampling basis this week: 3 largest by churn (63739975 2754 — almost entirely generated migration snapshots; 78881f65 1473; 1515380b 1364); 3 mid-distribution chosen by "feature commits carrying branching/seam logic near the 400–650 churn band" (23470206, 0dc4c979, 85e5cd3d — basis varied from last week's median-feature pick to stay unpredictable); 2 releases (§3 / §6); 2 patrol-produced (44123b3e ratchetwatch decomposition child of warren-5bf4; 1466ae81 gatewatch-remediation child of warren-00c8). Both releases judged separately for Article III.

Substance notes: craft is strong. 1515380b ships genuinely adversarial Article IV tests (corrupt `lastAttemptAt` never strands; `max_retries` precedence over `cooldown`; cooldown boundary at/after window) — verification, not theater. 23470206 pairs a 264-line renderer with a 258-line test. 85e5cd3d's new `bridge-reconnect.ts` lines are a MODIFICATION of a pre-existing file (verified `git cat-file -e 85e5cd3d^:src/server/bridge-reconnect.ts`), not a silent new module — no scope creep. The two "diverges" are isolated process findings, both already independently caught by gatewatch (warren-04dc/warren-6a91; warren-3c4d) — a precision signal, not new failures.

PRIOR-DIGEST FOLLOW-UP (resolved): last week's single systemic divergence — tracked `.pi/sessions/*.jsonl` transcripts riding unrelated commits (5/10 of the 06-14 sample) — is GONE. Zero session transcripts appear in any of this week's 72 commits or 10-sample diffs; the `.gitignore` fix (#401) landed. The 06-14 rate was inflated by that one cause; with it fixed the real divergence floor drops sharply (see §2).

## 2. Divergence rate

This week: 2/10 = 20%. Last week: 5/10 = 50%. The drop is real, not cosmetic: last week's 5 all shared ONE now-fixed systemic cause (`.pi/sessions` leak); this week's 2 are unrelated, isolated, and already population-flagged. Substantive craft was clean in both windows — the headline number moved because the systemic leak was closed.

## 3. Most important divergence — grandfather-at-birth in decomposition PRs (Article II), a recurring fix-on-fix class

44123b3e (#461, 06-21) decomposed `src/diagnostics/checks.ts`; in `biome.json` (override list ~line 80) it MOVED the `noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity` exemption from `checks.ts` to the NEWBORN `src/diagnostics/checks-config.ts` — a file that did not exist before the PR — directly violating Article II ("Nothing is grandfathered at birth: a new file written over the limit is decomposed before merge, not exempted at write time"). This is the THIRD identical instance in the run-up: 938d21bc (#391) birthed `pr-checks.ts` exempted, fba09fff (#436) birthed `in-flight.ts` exempted. gatewatch caught all three (warren-eb77, warren-2484, warren-04dc) and meta-flagged the pattern (warren-6a91); each was then remediated by a same-window complexity refactor within ~24–48h (fb04b24f, 6fba588b, and 1466ae81 — all 06-22). That is a textbook fix-on-fix chain. Named class: **decompose-then-grandfather-then-refactor** — the decomposition procedure carries complexity/size overrides FORWARD onto newborn siblings instead of refactoring inline, guaranteeing a follow-up refactor PR per split. The missing piece is a single executable gate (§5).

Secondary divergence (sample row 1466ae81, Article I): the very commit that remediated in-flight.ts merged green-by-bypass — body verbatim "Pre-commit verify hook bypassed (--no-verify): the only failing gate is a pre-existing, unrelated failure in src/runs/spawn/plot-append.test.ts". Article I names exactly this ("'this failure is unrelated' is a finding, not a waiver"). gatewatch filed it with full evidence (warren-3c4d, open); the flaky test was independently repaired the next day in 84d6a3f4 (#481), which does not retroactively sanction the bypass. Folded here, not re-filed — gatewatch owns it.

## 4. Auditor-population precision (findings filed since the 06-14 digest, 06-15 → 06-28)

- **ratchetwatch:** ~37 filed (12 weekly "tightening: <date>" rollups + ~25 concrete decompose/extract/floor tasks). 34 closed, **all closed-as-fixed** (their `[plan done]` decompositions landed: warren-5bf4→44123b3e, warren-895b→8c65ce62, warren-5f55/c2dc→e46e5a6f/0c3a740d, warren-ac7f→f31ad593, etc.), 0 closed-wontfix, 3 still open (warren-afe0/1b11/2dae — this week's rollups awaiting their children). **Closed-precision 34/34 = 100% fixed.** Second consecutive 100%-fixed digest.
- **gatewatch:** 8 findings filed (warren-172e, a19d, 9705, 2484, eb77, 04dc, 6a91, 3c4d). 4 closed — **all closed-as-fixed** (the grandfather-at-birth class warren-2484/eb77/04dc + meta warren-6a91, remediated by the 06-22 refactors), 0 wontfix, 4 still open (warren-172e/a19d/9705 title↔diff mismatches + warren-3c4d red-gate, awaiting human/process triage — none are stale-false, they are unactioned process findings). **Closed-precision 4/4 = 100% fixed.** Note the quality: gatewatch independently pre-flagged BOTH of this digest's sampled divergences (§3) before tastewatch sampled them — zero false positives observed this window.

Autonomy-promotion read: this is the SECOND consecutive digest with both auditors at 100% closed-as-fixed, 0 wontfix — the ≥2-digest trend the 06-14 digest said to wait for. ratchetwatch's signal is mechanical and consistently landed; gatewatch's is process/judgment and consistently true. RECOMMENDATION (advisory only, per Article IX / warden "Autonomy-promotion recommendations"): tastewatch now supports advancing ratchetwatch toward a scoped autonomy increment (its output is deterministic decomposition with a perfect landing record); hold gatewatch one more cycle only because its open findings are process-class (title/diff, red-gate) that need human disposition, not a precision concern. Any change to `.canopy/` or `.warren/triggers.yaml` requires explicit human review — delivered to the warden for routing, not applied.

## 5. Proposed gate (one; propose-only per Article IX)

Add `check:no-grandfather-at-birth` to `scripts/check-all.ts` (and CI). For each path newly added to `biome.json`'s `noExcessiveCognitiveComplexity` override list OR to `scripts/file-size-budgets.json` in a PR, fail if that path did not exist on the merge base — concretely, `git cat-file -e <base>:<path>` must succeed (the file pre-existed) for any added exemption entry; a newborn path in either exemption list is a hard fail. This converts Article II's manual "nothing grandfathered at birth" judgment — and gatewatch's recurring warren-6a91 finding — into the executable gate the constitution says every article aspires to, and it structurally ends the decompose-then-grandfather-then-refactor fix-on-fix chain (§3). Optional one-line Article II addendum: "a decomposition that exempts a newborn sibling is grandfathering-at-birth and is rejected; refactor the split inline." Proposed, not applied.

## 6. Trajectory

Tightening — the one systemic leak from 06-14 is closed, divergence halved to isolated process findings, both releases consumer-observable (v0.9.7 feat(dispatch)/feat(alerts)/feat(config); v0.9.8 a real plot-staging behavior fix), test craft is adversarial, and the audit population is running at 100% closed-as-fixed precision with gatewatch pre-catching tastewatch's own sample.

WARREN_API_TOKEN is now present (warren-f248 fixed), so the 401 blocker from the 06-14 digest is resolved; the remaining gap is the missing warden conversation. Per report-only mandate I did not create the conversation (that would be a new path). This seed is the durable record.

title: Runs sweep an unintended .canopy/agent.json provider/model flip into PRs, blocking Article IX auto-merge
description:
A run for an unrelated seed (warren-1d4c, a server eslint-comment chore) shipped PR jayminwest/warren#543 with a stray .canopy/agent.json diff flipping the builtin agent from anthropic/claude-opus-4-8 to zai/glm-5.2. Because .canopy/ is a constitution-protected path, auto-merge.yml's Article IX guard refused to arm auto-merge ("auto-merge will NOT be enabled: .canopy/agent.json"), so the PR needs a human merge and plan-run plnr_1bw1cw8ch4n6 (plan pl-4d2e) stalled. Every cleanup-batch child PR carries this same protected-path diff.

ROOT CAUSE (traced):
Write site: src/runs/seed.ts buildSeedFiles() unconditionally pushes a workspace file at path ".canopy/agent.json" containing the rendered AgentDefinition envelope { name, version, sections, resolvedFrom, frontmatter }. The serialized frontmatter carries the EFFECTIVE provider/model resolved in src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts (resolveOverride over defaultProvider/defaultModel), which is now zai/glm-5.2 after the provider-default switch.

Collision: the warren repo TRACKS .canopy/agent.json at HEAD as the builtin pi envelope (provider anthropic, model claude-opus-4-8). When warren operates on itself, the seed drop overwrites that tracked file with zai/glm-5.2, leaving a modified tracked file in the working tree.

Leak into the PR: PR #543 has two commits -
  - 136ea508f  author "Warren" (the agent's WARREN_GIT_AUTHOR identity), "chore(server): remove stale eslint-disable comment (#541)" -> touches .canopy/agent.json, .seeds/issues.jsonl, .seeds/plans.jsonl, src/server/main/index.ts
  - ee9978343  author warren <warren@os-eco.dev> (reap bookkeeping bot), .seeds/* only
The stray .canopy/agent.json flip is in the AGENT's commit, not warren's reap commit. The agent (system prompt: "Use git as you normally would. Commit your changes") ran a broad git add -A / git commit -a and swept the warren-seeded .canopy/agent.json modification in alongside its intended one-line edit. Reap staging (src/runs/reap/stage.ts) uses scoped git add -- <pathspec>, so reap is NOT the culprit.

FIX OPTIONS:
1. At provision, write the seed drop paths (.canopy/, .mulch/, .seeds/workflow.txt, .pi/) into the worktree .git/info/exclude so the agent's git add -A cannot stage them. NOTE: exclude does not cover an already-tracked file.
2. For repos that already track a seed path (warren-on-warren, canopy-library repos): skip seeding that path, or run git update-index --assume-unchanged on it post-seed so the seeded clobber never shows as a working-tree modification.
3. Combine 1+2: exclude for untracked drops, assume-unchanged for tracked ones.

Refs: plan-run plnr_1bw1cw8ch4n6, PR jayminwest/warren#543, src/runs/seed.ts, src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts, .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml (Article IX guard).
closeReason: Fixed by warren-8d95 (PR #599, commit 509ae7d7): finalize now resets seeded .canopy/agent.json to base bytes before branch_push, so the provider/model flip can no longer ride into PRs

title: Plan-run merge gate mis-maps transient GitHub 401/403/429 to pr_closed_without_merge
description: src/plan-runs/merge-gate.ts isFatalHttpError() returns true for ANY 4xx (status >= 400 && < 500). src/plan-runs/in-flight.ts:319 (and merge-gate.ts:114) then treat a fatal http_error identically to closed_unmerged and call failChild(..., 'pr_closed_without_merge'). A transient GitHub 401 (confirmed intermittent: 1 probe 401 then 6/6 200, /user 200, rate limit healthy) on the merge-status poll killed plan-run plnr_1bw1cw8ch4n6 at seq 1 even though PR #543 was OPEN/CLEAN/MERGEABLE (plan_run.failed event carried httpStatus:401). Fix: narrow isFatalHttpError to 404/410 and/or add 401/403/429 to the pr-merge retry set.

title: warren-bbde cannot be completed as written: its 92.98 lines floor would break CI (measurement was inflated by a deps-missing sandbox)
description:
Filed while working warren-bbde (plan pl-bb94, parent warren-acd7 "ratchetwatch tightening: 2026-07-01"). warren-bbde instructs raising the coverage `lines` floor in scripts/coverage-budgets.json from 91.54 -> 92.98 and updating the `_comment` baseline note to "functions 90.08%, lines 93.23% as of 2026-07-01". NOT applied — it would break CI.

## Root cause: the 93.23% baseline is inflated, not a lower bound

The patrol measured `bun run check:coverage` in a sandbox with MISSING node_modules (no `bun install` had been run). In that state, ~208 test files FAIL TO IMPORT ("Cannot find package 'drizzle-orm' / 'zod' / '@os-eco/burrow-cli' / ..."). When a test file fails to import, Bun's coverage reporter NEVER IMPORTS the source under test, so that source is EXCLUDED from the coverage denominator. A smaller denominator INFLATES the percentage. Hence the sandbox reported lines 93.23% — an inflated upper bound, not a lower bound.

The parent seed (warren-acd7) asserts: "The ~208 sandbox test failures are burrow-dependent and only DEPRESS coverage (93.23% is a lower bound); CI runs them green and measures >= 93.23%, so 92.98 passes." The direction of the effect is INVERTED. The failures do not depress coverage — they exclude source from the denominator and inflate it.

## Empirical proof (deps-installed == CI state)

CI runs `bun install` then `bun run check:coverage:ci` (= `scripts/check-coverage.ts --junit`, full `bun test --coverage`, no test filter). After `bun install` in this sandbox — which is exactly CI's state — ALL tests pass (3075 pass, 0 fail, 3091 tests across 322 files; the burrow integration tests pass because `@os-eco/burrow-cli` ships a `burrow` binary via node_modules/.bin/burrow). The only env-gated skips are 4 Postgres `describe.skipIf` blocks, and CI's workflow provisions no Postgres, so they're skipped in CI too. Measured "All files" row:

    functions 90.19% (floor 89.36%), lines 92.21% (floor 91.54%)

With the CURRENT floor (91.54), `bun run check:coverage` exits 0 (green): 92.21% >= 91.54%, no below-floor message. - lines:     slack = 92.21 - 91.54 = 0.67pt  -> UNDER 0.75pt -> NOT a finding (do NOT raise)

title: Capacity-aware admission control: derive per-worker run concurrency from host RAM / per-run memory budget
description: Follow-up to the 2026-07-07 OOM crash loop (burrow-2083, post-mortem in os-eco notes/2026-07-07-warren-deployed-oom-crash-loop-postmortem.md). burrow v0.3.15 caps each sandbox via cgroup v2 memory.max, but nothing stops warren dispatching N concurrent runs whose caps sum past host RAM. Placement (src/runs/placement.ts) should admit runs by capacity: concurrency_per_worker = floor((host RAM - overhead) / per-run memory budget), queueing the rest.
closeReason: Superseded by K8s migration plan pl-829f (parent warren-e176). Admission control is redesigned K8s-native (queue-depth + max-pending-pods + per-project cap) in warren-b6f2 step 21, and fail-fast is inherent to pod-per-run (pod-watcher sees OOMKilled in ~1-2s, replacing the 45-min watchdog). The burrow-era per-worker-concurrency and bridge_fatal approaches are obsolete; not built for the Fly/burrow path being retired.

title: Fail fast on bridge_fatal from unreachable worker instead of waiting the 45-min heartbeat watchdog
description: During the 2026-07-07 incident, bridge_fatal ('pinned to unreachable worker') left runs state=running with activeBridges=0; plan-runs looped waiting_for_run until the 45-min watchdog. burrow v0.3.15 adds an explicit oom_killed system event + 'sandbox memory limit exceeded' failure reason - warren should consume that signal, and consider reaping runs whose bridge died fatally once the worker is confirmed unreachable.
closeReason: Superseded by K8s migration plan pl-829f (parent warren-e176). The burrow-era per-worker-concurrency and bridge_fatal approaches are obsolete; not built for the Fly/burrow path being retired.

title: K8s migration design doc: pod-per-run isolation to replace single-Machine Fly co-tenancy
description: Strategic direction from the 2026-07-07 OOM post-mortem: move warren deployment to Kubernetes sooner rather than later. Deliverable: design doc evaluating pod-per-run isolation (pod boundary as the sandbox) or a runtime class (gVisor/Kata) vs porting the four bwrap security overrides (which managed k8s refuses, per fly.toml notes). Covers per-pod resource requests/limits, scheduler-owned placement, and how warren's existing multi-worker layer (workers table, placement.ts, BurrowClientPool) maps onto it.

Done when: src/workspace/git/exec.ts exists, tests green, check:all passes.

description: Phase EXTRACT. description: Phase CONTRACT (checkpoint 2). Create src/runtime/contract.ts with the RuntimeProvider interface and ALL types, no implementation: RunHandle (runId/sandboxId/providerRunId), RunSpec (incl. promoted baseBranch, domain-only env, network/resources intent), NormalizedEvent (seq/ts/kind/stream/payload, lossless), StreamOpts, RunPhase, TerminalReason (incl. oom_killed, lost), RunStatus (incl. exists, lastEventSeq/Ts), OutboundMessage, Message, RuntimeCapabilities, TeardownResult, FinalizeIntent, FinalizeResult. title: Implement LocalProvider.create() — collapse burrow burrows.up + runs.create into one op; map RunSpec→burrow; provider-owned callback URL

Implement LocalProvider.create(spec): collapse burrow's two calls (client.burrowsUp then client.http.runs.create) into one op behind the seam; map RunSpec to the burrow requests; compute the callback URL provider-side (loopback for Local) rather than from domain env. Return a RunHandle. Depends on steps 5,7. Ref: runtime-provider-contract.md section 6 items 1,3. Done when: create dispatches a real burrow run via the seam, tests green.

title: Implement LocalProvider.streamEvents() + status() — wrap burrow SSE + runs.get; normalize NormalizedEvent; map exists/terminalReason (surface OOM warren currently drops)
description: Phase CONTRACT. Implement LocalProvider.streamEvents() (wrap burrow SSE, yield NormalizedEvent with burrow seq, lossless payload, resume via sinceSeq) and status() (wrap runs.get, map to RunStatus, return exists:false instead of throwing on 404, set terminalReason incl. oom_killed from burrow's OOM signal warren currently discards). Depends on step 7. Ref: runtime-provider-contract.md sections 1-2, corrections 5,7. Done when: bridge consumes events through the seam identically, tests green.

title: Implement LocalProvider.sendMessage() — wrap burrow inbox.send; map OutboundMessage/Message with priority + FIFO
description: Phase CONTRACT. Implement LocalProvider.sendMessage(handle, msg) wrapping client.http.inbox.send; honor body/priority/fromActor; return the persisted Message row; preserve priority-desc then FIFO ordering and unread/delivered/failed lifecycle. Depends on step 7. Ref: runtime-provider-contract.md steering section. Done when: steer works through the seam, tests green.

title: Implement LocalProvider.cancel() + terminate() — wrap POST /cancel + burrows.destroy; return TeardownResult
description: Phase CONTRACT. Implement LocalProvider.cancel(handle, reason) wrapping POST /runs/:id/cancel, and terminate(handle) wrapping client.http.burrows.destroy(archive:true) returning TeardownResult (archived + deleted counts). Keep cancel and terminate distinct. Depends on step 7. Ref: runtime-provider-contract.md sections 3-4. Done when: cancel and reap teardown work through the seam, tests green.

title: Implement LocalProvider.finalize() as a host-side wrapper over the existing reap pipeline; pin down FinalizeResult mirror-delta shapes (mulch/seeds/plans/plot; keep plot thin per data-plane-trajectory)

Implement LocalProvider.finalize(handle, intent) as a thin host-side wrapper over the EXISTING reap pipeline (mergeMulch, mirrorSeeds, mirrorPlans, mergePlot, push, commits-ahead, empty-push) with zero behavior change. Critically: define the FinalizeResult mirror-delta shapes (MulchDelta/SeedsDelta/PlansDelta/PlotDelta) by serializing today's in-process merge outputs; these are consumed by the K8s in-pod finalize (step 20). Keep PlotDelta thin/disposable per docs/design/data-plane-trajectory.md. Depends on step 7. Ref: runtime-provider-contract.md section 4. Done when: reap runs through finalize with parity, delta types defined, tests green.

title: Route domain call-sites (dispatch, stream/bridge, watchdog, steer, reap) through RuntimeProvider; CHECKPOINT 2 — verify behavioral parity with check:all green and a real LocalProvider run

Refactor domain call-sites to depend on RuntimeProvider, not burrow-client: dispatch.ts (create), stream/bridge.ts + stream/* (streamEvents/status), watchdog.ts (status; keep the mode-exclusion in the domain), steer.ts (sendMessage), reap/* (finalize THEN terminate, in that order). Keep watchdog/heartbeat, failure_reason derivation, budget caps, and pause state IN the domain (anti-leak line, contract section 3). Depends on steps 8,9,10,11,12. Done when: with WARREN_RUNTIME=local warren reproduces today's behavior exactly, a real run passes end-to-end, and check:all is green. Do NOT start phase 3 on a red checkpoint.

title: Implement pod-watcher informer → status()/phase reconciliation (OOMKilled→terminalReason, NotFound→exists:false); add pod-phase/oom/pending/init Prometheus metrics + ServiceMonitor

Add Prometheus metrics warren_run_pod_phase, warren_run_oom_killed_total, warren_pod_pending_duration_seconds, warren_workspace_init_duration_seconds, plus a ServiceMonitor. Depends on step 14. Ref: k8s-migration.md 1.3/3.2/5.2. Done when: watcher drives run state within ~1-2s of pod termination, metrics exported, tests green.

title: Implement K8sProvider.streamEvents() — follow pod logs, parse NDJSON, synthesize monotonic per-run seq cursor with resume

Implement K8sProvider.sendMessage() writing to run_inbox. Depends on step 14. Ref: k8s-migration.md 1.4. Done when: an in-pod poll delivers a steer within ~5s, tests green.

Depends on steps 14,16. Ref: k8s-migration.md R6, runtime-provider-contract.md section 4. Done when: cancel stops a run, terminate + GC reclaim pods, tests green.

Done when: a K8s run pushes its branch and mirrors seeds/mulch to the project clone with no shared filesystem, proven in step 25.

title: Implement K8s-native admission control (queue-depth 429, max-pending-pods, per-project concurrency cap); supersede warren-b01e + warren-ea4f

description: Found during warren-fd08 live validation. Run state is committed before the crash so terminalization is durable, but the control plane bounces on every k8s run teardown. Likely fix: defensively catch/swallow the expected AbortError in the log-follow teardown path; add a unit test around abort-during-follow. Runs still complete — stability bug, not a correctness blocker.

scheduler/plan-run/merge-poller spawn bypasses runtime provider — K8s cron dispatches fail never_started every tick
description: bootScheduler, createPlanRunSpawn, and createMergePollerDispatch called spawnRun without threading the resolved runtimeProvider, so under WARREN_RUNTIME=k8s they fell back to the burrow-backed LocalProvider and every scheduled dispatch failed never_started against the absent burrow socket. Observed on GKE: nightwatch-patrol cron produced ~200 failed runs in 3h (one per 60s tick — transient-failure retry semantics never consume the slot). warren-c531 threaded the provider into bridges/poller/watchdog but missed these three spawn wrappers. Fix: thread runtimeProvider through all three + boot wiring in server/main/index.ts and detector-wiring.ts.

title: scheduler: bound transient spawn-failure retries — back off / consume slot after N attempts, stop minting a failed run row per tick
description: dispatchCronTrigger treats any non-agent-not-found spawn failure as transient and retries every 60s tick within the same slot, and spawnRun creates the run row before contacting the runtime, so a persistently-unreachable runtime (e.g. the pre-warren-1ca1 K8s misconfig, or burrow down for hours) mints one failed/never_started run row per tick indefinitely (~200 rows in 3h observed on GKE). Harden: (1) cap in-slot retries or add exponential backoff per trigger, consuming the slot after N consecutive transient failures with a scheduler.cron_gave_up log; (2) consider not persisting (or GC-ing) never_started rows from scheduler retries so the runs list isn't flooded. Keep genuine brief-outage retry behavior (pl-2f15 risk #5) intact.

title: warren bot commits are not immune to inherited GIT_AUTHOR_*/GIT_COMMITTER_* env — breaks Article VII + fails clone-apply test under pre-commit hook
description: warrenCommitIdentityArgs() pins the bot identity via '-c user.name/user.email', but git's GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL env vars take precedence over config. Any warren process inheriting those vars mis-authors the reap bookkeeping commits (stage.ts x2, clone-apply.ts) and the plot-sync commit (plots/sync.ts) as the operator instead of 'warren <warren@os-eco.dev>'. Concrete repro: 'git commit' exports GIT_AUTHOR_* to its hooks, so this repo's own pre-commit (check:all -> bun test) deterministically fails clone-apply.test.ts 'commits as the warren bot' on every local commit; GIT_AUTHOR_NAME='x' bun test src/runs/reap/clone-apply.test.ts reproduces directly. Fix: add warrenCommitIdentityEnv() to src/bot-identity.ts (explicit GIT_AUTHOR_/GIT_COMMITTER_ name+email), extend ReapExec.run opts and projects/clone.ts SpawnFn options with optional env, and pass the identity env at the four commit sites so inherited env can never win.

RESULTS (2026-07-16, k8s-migration @ dfa3d7df, macOS/Docker Desktop): ALL THREE PARTS PASS. Part 1: bun run acceptance --only 04,05,07,08,09,10 → 6/6 (real burrow serve + warren over unix socket: dispatch, events stream, steer, cancel, reap mulch+seeds roundtrips). title: K8s agent-entrypoint breaks pi runtime: stdin closed at spawn, agent exits before doing any work
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Adopted into plan pl-829f.

Parent seed: warren-e176 — K8s migration design doc: pod-per-run isolation to replace single-Machine Fly co-tenancy
Plan template: feature

<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

Dogfood run run_nejha296p9es (pi agent, WARREN_RUNTIME=k8s) exited 0 ~2s after launch having emitted only the prompt-ack event — no work, no commit — yet reported 'succeeded'. Root cause: src/runtime/k8s/agent-entrypoint.ts defaultSpawn writes command.stdin then unconditionally proc.stdin.end(). Burrow's pi runtime contract (burrow-cli src/runtime/pi.ts) requires the dispatcher to HOLD STDIN OPEN until pi emits agent_end (shouldCloseStdinOnEvent seam) — pi exits the instant stdin closes, even mid-inference. Burrow documents this exact signature as burrow-5db3 ('only response+agent_start+turn_start and exit 0 with no assistant content'). Fix: implement the stdin-hold seam in the K8s entrypoint spawn loop (honor runtime.shouldCloseStdinOnEvent, keep stdin open, close on terminal envelope), mirroring burrow's dispatcher (dispatch.ts holdStdin path). This also unblocks mid-run steering for stdin-held runtimes on K8s. Until fixed, pi/leveret/healer builtins silently no-op under WARREN_RUNTIME=k8s.

description:

run_nejha296p9es: pod completed 16:06 UTC; warren's run-state poller logged 'run-state poller observed burrow terminal; draining stream before abort' (terminalReason=completed, exit 0) and then NOTHING — 40+ min later the run row still shows state=running, endedAt=null. No reap, no finalize, no failureReason. Two compounding defects: (1) the stream drain after terminal observation has no bound and appears to hang forever, leaving the run non-terminal; (2) the in-pod finalize handshake deadlocks — the pod's finalize-entrypoint polled GET /runs/:id/finalize-intent every 2s for exactly its 300s budget and always got {intent:null}, because warren only parks the intent at reap time, and warren only detected terminal by observing POD EXIT (pi emitted no agent_end terminal envelope, see warren-7a43) — which only happened when the pod's finalize gave up. Pod waits on warren, warren waits on pod: 5 wasted minutes, then no FinalizeResult ever posted, so no branch push / workspace collection. Fix: bound the drain; make reap park the finalize intent (or fail with the documented finalize-timeout FinalizeResult path) when terminal is observed via pod exit; add a watchdog that force-fails runs whose pod is terminal but whose row stays running. Immediate ops mitigation: force-cancel run_nejha296p9es. Related minor noise: pod-log follow reconnect-loops every 15s with 'disconnected while pod live' the whole time a pod is Pending.

title: GKE Autopilot capacity model: baseline eats SSD quota, first run stalls 5min on scale-up — weigh Autopilot vs alternatives
description: RESOLUTION 2026-07-21: 750GB retry also auto-denied (traceId b210aa6b). Quantified the capacity model: SSD_TOTAL_GB usage is 455/500, of which only 55GB is PVCs (5GB + 50GB pd-balanced) — the other ~400GB is Autopilot node boot disks (100GB pd-balanced each), which count against SSD quota. DISKS_TOTAL_GB (pd-standard) is 0/4096 — untouched. DECISION: stay on GKE Autopilot; the fix is not the quota but decoupling node boot disks from SSD quota via a custom ComputeClass (storage.bootDiskType pd-standard, or smaller bootDiskSize) so scale-up draws from the 4TB standard-disk pool. Quota retry window reopens 2026-07-23 ~16:00Z (48h cooldown) as a secondary lever. reap(k8s): finalize timeout still reports run succeeded and destroys workspace — agent work silently lost
description:
Evidence: run_r3fys9c24dg1 (2026-07-17, app.warren.run, seed warren-9cda). In-pod finalize timed out after 120000ms; ALL finalize steps failed (mulch_merge, seeds_close, plans_mirror, plot_merge, plot_commit, seeds_commit, branch_push — reap.completed.errors[]), branchPushed:false, prUrl:null, commitsAhead:null. Despite this, reap.completed recorded state:'succeeded' and reap.workspace_destroyed followed, deleting the pod workspace holding the only copy of the agent's commit (a2315c83, the warren-9cda fix). seedIdClosed:true was even recorded host_side (fortunately seeds_commit failed so the close never landed). Likely triggered under GKE quota pressure with 3 concurrent runs.

Expected behavior: (1) when finalize times out/fails before branch_push completes, the run must NOT be reported succeeded — mark it failed or a distinct reap-failed terminal state with failureReason populated; (2) do not destroy the workspace when branchPushed:false and the agent made commits — preserve or archive it so work is recoverable; (3) skip host-side seed close when the push failed; (4) consider making the 120s in-pod finalize timeout configurable and/or retrying finalize once before declaring loss.

Relevant code: reap core FinalizeResult consumption (warren-fbbf / PR #589), k8s provider in-pod finalize, reap workspace destruction. Acceptance: a run whose finalize times out before branch_push ends non-succeeded, keeps (or archives) its workspace, surfaces reap errors via GET /runs/:id, and does not close its seed.

title: workspace seeding overwrites tracked .canopy/agent.json — agent commits sweep it into PRs and trip the Article IX automerge guard
description:
Evidence: run_a1j8jp04g6t5 (plan-run plnr_w0en7cy80q5s child for warren-2141, PR #597). Warren seeds the rendered agent definition to /workspace/.canopy/agent.json. In projects that themselves use canopy (warren's own repo tracks .canopy/agent.json), this overwrites a TRACKED file, leaving the worktree dirty; a broad agent commit (git add -A / commit -a) then carries the seeded artifact into the PR. The auto-merge workflow's Article IX protected-path guard (regex includes ^\.canopy/) correctly refused to enable auto-merge, so the PR sat unmerged and the plan-run failed with child_pr_merge_timeout. Remediation applied by hand: reverted .canopy/agent.json to base on the PR branch (commit 0c3d6caa).

Fix directions (pick the robust one): (1) seed the rendered agent definition to a non-colliding path outside the repo worktree (e.g. /workspace/.warren-agent/agent.json or an env-pointed tmp path) and update the workspace map prompt accordingly; (2) if it must live at .canopy/agent.json, mark it excluded from git in the workspace (git update-index --skip-worktree or .git/info/exclude won't help for tracked files — reap should instead git checkout the seeded paths back to base before commit/push); (3) at minimum, reap's finalize should reset warren-seeded artifact paths before branch_push so they never ride along.

Acceptance: a run against a project that tracks .canopy/agent.json produces a PR whose diff does NOT include .canopy/agent.json (unless the agent intentionally edited it), and the auto-merge Article IX guard passes on runs that only touch non-protected paths.

title: plan-run child seeds not reliably auto-closed when the child PR merges
description:
Observed on plan-run plnr_8g1crv7f47xp (pl-bb94, 2026-07-17): children warren-3f09 and warren-f854 reached state 'merged' (PRs #602/#603 automerged) but their seeds remained open — neither the agent (default promptTemplate 'work on sd {seed_id}' does not instruct closing) nor warren's host-side close (reap seedIdClosed, which DID fire host_side for single-run run_r3fys9c24dg1) closed them. Meanwhile the pl-2737 child run for warren-0f57 closed its seed only because the agent itself committed 'chore: close warren-0f57'. Result: seed closure after a merged plan-run child is nondeterministic — depends on agent initiative. Operator had to close 3f09/f854 manually.

Expected: when a plan-run child's PR merges (the child state transition to 'merged'), warren should deterministically close the child's seed (host-side commit to the project's default branch, using WARREN_BOT_IDENTITY per Article VII), or the default plan-run promptTemplate should instruct closure — pick one canonical mechanism so it does not depend on the agent. Acceptance: a plan-run whose children all merge leaves all child seeds closed with no operator action; single-run seedId close behavior unchanged.

title: reap: intentional no-commit runs misclassified as dropped_commit; host-side seedIdClosed fires on failed runs
description: Evidence: run_t5nz6w2tbxj5 and run_74ytqab5zz85 (2026-07-17, seed warren-d182). The agent deliberately made NO commits (it determined the seed's premise was stale and said so in its final message), leaving some uncommitted analysis/bookkeeping files in the workspace. Reap emitted reap.empty_push {dirty:true, droppedCommit:true, message:'git push exited zero and the workspace still has uncommitted changes — agent staged work but never committed'} and failed the run with failureReason=dropped_commit. Two issues: (1) CLASSIFICATION — a dirty workspace with zero commits ahead is not necessarily a dropped commit; when the agent's result message indicates intentional no-op (or when the only dirty paths are bookkeeping artifacts like .mulch/), reap should distinguish 'agent declined to change anything' (a legitimate outcome, arguably succeeded-with-no-diff or a distinct no_changes terminal) from 'agent work lost'. The dropped_commit guard (warren-495d) is right to be conservative, but two identical intentional-no-op runs both surfacing as infra failures cost an operator investigation. (2) SEED CLOSE ON FAILURE — reap emitted seeds.seed_id_closed {mode:host_side} for warren-d182 even though the run FAILED and the agent explicitly declined to close the seed; only the (unrelated) seeds_commit not landing kept the close from persisting. Host-side seedIdClosed must not fire for runs that end failed/cancelled. Acceptance: a run whose agent makes no commits and states an intentional no-op ends in a non-alarming terminal state distinct from dropped_commit, and host-side seed close never fires on failed runs.

title: auto-merge Article IX guard: file list capped at 100 entries — protected paths invisible on large PRs; no opt-out label for human-gated PRs
description: Two related gaps in .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml observed on PR #609 (k8s-migration → main, 410 files). (1) PAGINATION: the guard computes CHANGED via 'gh pr view --json files', which returns at most 100 files; on a >100-file PR, a protected path (docs/CONSTITUTION.md, .warren/triggers.yaml, .canopy/, auto-merge.yml) positioned beyond the cap would not match and auto-merge would be wrongly enabled. Fix: use the paginated files API ('gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/files --paginate -q .[].path') or 'gh pr diff --name-only'. (2) NO HUMAN-GATE OPT-OUT: the workflow enables auto-merge on ANY PR without protected paths, and re-runs on every synchronize — for PR #609 it enabled auto-merge against the PR author's explicit 'Do NOT auto-merge' intent (operator had to gh pr merge --disable-auto). Add an opt-out: skip enablement when the PR carries a 'no-automerge' label (or 'do-not-merge' in title), so human-gated PRs stay human-gated across pushes. Acceptance: a 400-file PR with a protected path in its final files is refused enablement; a PR labeled no-automerge is never enabled, including after synchronize.
closeReason: Fixed directly on k8s-migration: enable-auto-merge job now skips PRs labeled 'no-automerge' (label created, applied to PR #609), and the Article IX guard reads changed files via the paginated pulls/files API instead of gh pr view --json files (100-entry cap).

title: K8s control plane: git auth for host-side clone/fetch/push (project_unavailable: could not read Username)
description: Under WARREN_RUNTIME=k8s, 'warren serve' runs without the supervisor, so the supervisor's global insteadOf rule (git-credentials.ts) never installs and every host-side git network op against a private repo died on git's interactive username prompt (exit 128). Fix: githubCredentialGitEnv (src/workspace/git/credential-env.ts) renders the same x-access-token insteadOf rule as GIT_CONFIG_* env vars, applied per-spawn via SpawnOptions.env at project clone, refresh fetch, spawnRun pre-dispatch refresh, plot-sync fetch/push, and plan-run seed-close fetch/push. Token source is AutoOpenPrConfig.gitToken (raw GITHUB_TOKEN, never the acceptance stub-token).

FinalizeIntent.mirror -> FinalizeIntent.artifacts: string[]; FinalizeResult.mirror -> FinalizeResult.artifacts: Record<string,ArtifactDelta>; InPodFinalizeIntent.mirror -> artifacts. Update BOTH providers (LocalProvider host-side + K8sProvider in-pod collection/wire/validation) and all consumers (reap pipeline applyFinalizeToState, clone-apply collectCloneWrites). The mulch/seeds/plans merges keep running exactly where the workspace lives (host-side local, in-pod K8s); behavior preserved — finalize just no longer names features in its contract types.

(2) Move the genuinely bus-movable piece onto the observation bus: the clone-side seed-close safety net (closeRunSeedId, which ran in the reap pipeline against the host clone, NOT inside provider.finalize) becomes a post_reap subscriber registered via the bus boot-time registration API (warren-bb60). title: K8s auto-plan-run loses newly-created Seeds before child dispatch
description:
Production evidence (app.warren.run, 2026-07-25): nightwatch run run_fheyyrtcfp7g created plan pl-c559 and children warren-dbda/warren-2fc2/warren-33c1/warren-8aa5/warren-267c. Reap emitted reap.clone_deltas_applied and auto_plan_run_created (plnr_4tn7zxf11crp), but branchPushed=true, commitsAhead=0, seedsCommitted=false. The first child pod cloned origin/main and could not find warren-dbda; the coordinator then failed seq 2 as child_seed_not_found:warren-2fc2.

Root cause: under K8s, the pod pushes its run branch before the control plane applies FinalizeResult mirror bodies. src/runs/reap/clone-apply.ts then authors `chore(warren): mirror state` only in the control-plane host clone; it does not push that commit or make it the plan-run ref. Production reflog proves f68ec53e was created at 09:08:45 with exactly 6 issue rows + pl-c559, had no containing ref after the incident, and was discarded by `reset: moving to origin/main` at 09:09:01. The auto-plan row was nevertheless created against that ephemeral host-only state. This also occurred on 2026-07-22 (plnr_a6km12v631hf and plnr_79qtd1vc179a).

Fix the K8s finalize/auto-dispatch ordering or durability contract so tracker deltas are reachable from the exact git ref child pods clone BEFORE an auto plan-run is created. Do not merely suppress child_seed_not_found: the new plan/issues must persist to origin. Preserve LocalProvider behavior.

Acceptance:
- K8s-style finalize with newly-created .seeds issue + plan rows makes them reachable from the plan-run ref before coordinator dispatch.
- First and later child workspaces can `sd show <child>` from their fresh clone.
- A host clone refresh/reset cannot discard the only copy of the mirrored rows.
- No auto_plan_run_created event/DB row is emitted if tracker durability fails.
- Regression test covers the K8s FinalizeResult -> clone delta -> auto-plan-run -> child-clone boundary, not only an in-memory repo stub.
closeReason: Fixed by PR #631 (merge commit cd726b74, MERGED 2026-07-25, on main): applyK8sCloneDeltas (src/runs/reap/clone-apply.ts:216) pushes the mirror commit before auto-dispatch, and mirrorDurabilityFailed suppresses auto_plan_run_created (pipeline.ts:312); regression test run.k8s.auto-plan-run.test.ts covers the child-clone boundary.

title: Release-created GitHub events never trigger GKE deploy
description: The documented release -> GKE deploy chain is broken. release.yml publishes the GitHub release with gh release create using GH_TOKEN=github.token. GitHub suppresses workflow runs caused by events created with GITHUB_TOKEN (except workflow_dispatch/repository_dispatch), so deploy-gke.yml never receives its release: published event. The release bump push does invoke GKE Build & Deploy, but deploy-gke.yml explicitly skips the deploy job for push events on main. Evidence for v0.10.1: release run 29847964848 published v0.10.1 at commit 37308a90; GKE run 29847964203 built images but deploy was skipped; no release-event GKE run exists. Last successful deploy was manual run 29793717932 at commit 4c65820a, leaving production on 0.10.0 while v0.10.1 was released. Fix with an explicit workflow_call/workflow_dispatch from release.yml (or a non-GITHUB_TOKEN release actor), ensure the exact release SHA is deployed, and add verification that the live image/version matches the release. Acceptance: publishing a release through release.yml causes a successful non-skipped GKE deploy for that exact SHA; a regression test/check prevents relying on a suppressed GITHUB_TOKEN-generated event; workflow fails visibly if rollout/version verification fails; docs describe the actual trigger path.

title: Child empty-push is scored as a trivial merge even when its seed never resolved
description:
In src/plan-runs/in-flight.ts:201-222 (resolveMissingPrUrl), a succeeded child with no PR URL is treated as a trivial merge whenever hasEmptyPushEvent() is true: the child transitions to state=merged with prMergedAt set and emits plan_run.merged {trivial:true}, and the plan advances.

That conflates 'the agent correctly had nothing to commit' with 'the agent could not do the work at all'. The child_succeeded_without_pr failure reason exists but is unreachable on this path, because the empty-push branch returns before resolveChildPrReopen is consulted.

Production evidence (app.warren.run, 2026-07-25, plnr_4tn7zxf11crp / pl-c559): child seq 1 warren-dbda ran as run_2vc5kmtn01xy, emitted reap.empty_push, and was recorded state=merged prMergedAt=2026-07-25T09:09:49.777Z. The agent's own final text was: 'The issue warren-dbda does not exist in this project's Seeds tracker. I verified this three ways: sd show warren-dbda -> Error: Issue not found; grep dbda .seeds/*.jsonl -> no matches; sd search dbda -> No issues match.' The run had prUrl=null, 900 output tokens, 42s wall clock.

So a child that failed for exactly the reason under investigation in warren-486c was scored as a success, and the plan-run only died one seq later at child_seed_not_found:warren-2fc2 -- a less informative error pointing at the wrong seed. This masks warren-486c in every report and makes the true first failure point invisible.

This is an amplifier of warren-486c, not a duplicate: even after seed durability is fixed, an agent that cannot find its seed for any other reason (typo'd id, wrong repo, unmerged branch) will still be scored as a successful trivial merge.

Fix: an empty push must only count as a trivial merge when the child's seed actually resolved in the run's workspace. When the seed did not resolve, fail the child with a typed reason that names the real cause rather than advancing the plan.

Acceptance:
- A child whose seed did not resolve in its workspace and which pushed nothing fails with a typed reason; it is NOT recorded as merged/trivial.
- A child whose seed DID resolve and legitimately had nothing to commit still merges trivially (no regression).
- The emitted event distinguishes the two cases so the UI and plan-run detail show the true first failure.
- Regression test covers the reap.empty_push + unresolved-seed combination end to end, not only an in-memory stub.

title: A single failed child fails the entire plan-run and strands all remaining children
description:
The plan-run coordinator is fail-fast: when any child reaches a terminal failure, src/plan-runs/coordinator.ts transitions the whole plan-run to failed and every remaining child is abandoned in state=pending. There is no retry, no skip-and-continue, and no resume of the untouched tail.

Production evidence (app.warren.run):
- plnr_va8n5w40hbjb (pl-3a79, 18 children): seqs 1-7 merged cleanly as PRs 616-622. Seq 8 (warren-b8bf, PR 624) hit child_pr_merge_timeout. Seqs 9-18 -- 10 children -- were never dispatched and were left pending forever.
- plnr_ns9v4mtc90v1 (pl-3f96, 5 children): seq 1 failed; seqs 2-5 stranded.
- plnr_4tn7zxf11crp (pl-c559, 5 children): seq 2 failed; seqs 3-5 stranded.

The blast radius is worst when the failing child's problem is unrelated to the rest of the plan. In plnr_va8n5w40hbjb the single blocker was PR 624 being closed unmerged; the other 10 children were independent work items that had nothing to do with it. Re-dispatching the plan does resume (closed children are skipped), but that is a manual operator action, and each re-dispatch re-fails on the same stuck child -- pl-3a79 was re-dispatched at least 4 times (plnr_exdp1zschr6v, plnr_va8n5w40hbjb, plnr_5db31y4yqd61, plnr_deda6rq9rq80) and never got past its blocked seq without human intervention.

Note this is a design change, not a bug fix, and it interacts with the plan-run's serial-by-design contract (SPEC 11.P gates each child on the previous PR merging). Independent children are the case worth relaxing; genuinely dependent ones must still stop.

Desired: a failed child should not automatically destroy the remaining tail. Options to weigh (pick one, do not build all):
- Continue past a failed child when the plan declares no dependency between it and the remaining children, recording the plan-run as partially failed.
- Bounded retry of a failed child before failing the plan.
- Keep fail-fast but leave the plan-run resumable so a re-dispatch skips the known-bad child instead of re-failing on it.

Acceptance:
- A plan-run with one failed independent child still completes its remaining independent children.
- A plan-run whose failed child blocks its successors still stops, and says so.
- The terminal plan-run state distinguishes 'fully succeeded' from 'completed with failures'.
- Operator can see which children were skipped or abandoned and why.
- SPEC 11.P is updated to describe the chosen semantics.
closeReason: Decision 2026-08-04: satisfied by the combination of warren-1eff (resume a failed plan-run past a merge-timeout) and warren-6de9 (one bounded retry on child_provider_error). No new terminal state or child dependency model — fail-fast stays, but a failure is no longer a dead end. Reopen only if resume+retry prove insufficient in practice.

title: finalize_failed silently discards all run work: no branch push, workspace destroyed, no recovery
description:
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:start -->
Step 10 of plan pl-1c02.

Parent seed: warren-24d0 — 0.13.x truth & hygiene batch — carried-over fixes, promotion completion, phase-0 hygiene
Plan template: feature
Plan approach: Work the batch as independent small PRs cut as 0.13.x patch releases, in the order set by seam-sequencing phase 0 + 0' remainders. Spawn new child seeds only for untracked work; adopt the already-tracked issues (warren-6fa0, warren-cd3b,…

Run `sd plan show pl-1c02` for the full plan (context, alternatives, sibling steps, acceptance criteria).
<!-- seeds:plan-backref:end -->

When a K8s run pod exits without posting a finalize result, reap emits "run pod reached a terminal phase without posting a finalize result; in-pod finalize could not run" and the run's ENTIRE output is lost: the run branch is never pushed, no PR is opened, and the workspace (an emptyDir, sizeLimit 10Gi) dies with the container. There is no retry, no salvage path, and no operator-visible warning beyond the failure reason.

Observed 2026-07-25 on app.warren.run, three times in ~25 minutes:
- run_3ervp71xxedr (pi, warren-486c): started 16:24:21, failed 16:55:38. 54,323 output tokens, $8.14. The agent had COMPLETED the fix and was running git commit with the check:all pre-commit hook at 16:46:59. All of it lost.
- run_jh56za9q0w8t (pi, warren-df0b): started 16:25:10, failed 16:58:16. 59,808 output tokens, $8.43. Same signature.
- run_6wx1sxg6r196 (bugwatch, cron): started 16:50:38, failed 16:51:26 after only 48s, $0.18.

Total measured loss: ~$16.75 and ~64 minutes of completed agent work in a single incident window.

In every case reap logged reap.workspace_destroy_skipped with reason branch_push_failed, and git ls-remote origin confirmed no run branch on origin -- so the work existed ONLY in the pod's emptyDir and was unrecoverable once the container exited.

SUSPECTED TRIGGER (not proven): a control-plane rollout. The first two runs were dispatched at 16:24-16:25 by the control-plane pod that was replaced at ~16:47 by a workflow_dispatch deploy; both then failed finalize afterward. A re-dispatch of the same seed with the same agent that did NOT span a rollout (run_xnsna0jvpecz, 16:57-17:14) succeeded normally and opened PR #631.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE -- do not assume the rollout is the only cause: run_6wx1sxg6r196 started at 16:50:38, ~3 minutes AFTER the new control plane was ready (pod start 16:47:49), spanned no rollout, and hit the identical signature after 48s. So this message is a generic "pod exited without finalizing" symptom with multiple possible causes (crash, OOM, early exit, severed callback), and the rollout hypothesis explains at most the two long runs. Investigate the symptom first; do not fix only the rollout case.

The durability defect is real regardless of trigger: warren treats "pod died before finalize" as an ordinary terminal failure and discards everything, when the agent's commits may be intact in the workspace at that moment.

Acceptance:
- A pod that exits without posting a finalize result does not silently lose committed work; warren attempts to push/salvage the run branch before destroying the workspace.
- Workspace destruction is gated on either successful salvage or an explicit unrecoverable determination, and the distinction is visible to the operator.
- The failure reason distinguishes root causes (callback unreachable / pod crashed / OOM / early exit) instead of collapsing them into one message.
- If a control-plane restart can sever in-pod finalize, either in-flight runs survive it or dispatch is drained/gated during rollout; document which.
- Regression coverage for the pod-exits-without-finalize path asserting committed work is not discarded.
closeReason: Salvage-before-destroy shipped: pod self-salvages (rescue ref + git-bundle POST to /runs/:id/salvage, retried through rollouts) in both loss windows; local reap salvages host-side before destroy and a captured work product lifts the preserve skip; location stamped on run row (salvage_ref/salvage_path) + reap.workspace_salvaged event; lost-finalize message now names phase+terminalReason; proven by src/runtime/k8s/finalize-entrypoint.salvage.test.ts, src/server/handlers/runs.salvage.test.ts, src/runs/reap/run.salvage.test.ts; 12/12 gates green

title: Cron patrol reliability: nightwatch succeeded only 38% in production — fix before re-enabling the trigger
description:
The scheduled patrol agents (nightwatch, bugwatch) are failing far more often than they succeed on app.warren.run. Across the 60 most recent runs as of 2026-07-25, only 6 of 19 cron-triggered runs succeeded (32%):

  nightwatch: 5 succeeded, 4 never_started, 3 crashed, 1 dropped_commit   (5/13, 38%)
  bugwatch:   1 succeeded, 3 dropped_commit, 1 finalize_failed, 1 never_started  (1/6, 17%)

These agents are the top of warren's autonomous funnel -- nightwatch and bugwatch produce the seeds plans that auto_plan_run then executes. A 32% success rate at the source means most scheduled patrol cycles produce nothing, silently, and no one is paged.

Four distinct failure modes, likely four different causes; triage separately:

1. never_started (5 runs) -- the pod never started at all. Suspect cluster capacity / quota; note warren-cca7 tracks SSD_TOTAL_GB sitting at 455/500 with agent-pod scale-up stalling on quota. If that is the cause, these runs are being dropped by admission or scheduling with no retry and should either retry with backoff or surface as an operator alert rather than a silent failed run.

2. dropped_commit (4 runs, both agents) -- the agent staged work but never ran git commit, so reap discards it. The builtin agent system prompt already warns about this explicitly ("git add ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH"), so either the instruction is not landing, or the agents are being terminated mid-commit (note run_1mmn0h0r5wxk hit this after an upstream Cloudflare 520 killed the session mid-work -- an API failure, not agent error). Worth distinguishing "agent forgot" from "agent was killed before it could commit", because the fixes differ.

3. crashed (3 nightwatch runs) -- uninvestigated; needs event-log triage.

4. finalize_failed (1 bugwatch run, run_6wx1sxg6r196) -- see warren-cd3b, which covers the durability defect behind this signature.

Investigate in that order; never_started and dropped_commit are 9 of the 13 failures between them.

Acceptance:
- Root cause identified for never_started, and either fixed or surfaced as an explicit operator-visible condition (alert / distinct state) rather than a silent failed run.
- dropped_commit runs distinguish "agent never committed" from "agent was terminated before committing"; the latter is retried or salvaged rather than discarded.
- The three crashed nightwatch runs are triaged and either fixed or filed as their own issue with event evidence.
- Cron agent success rate is measurable -- add a metric or report so this regression is visible next time instead of needing a manual run-list audit.

---
UPDATE 2026-07-28 (warren-a781 cleanup): NOT urgent — nothing is scheduled. Every cron
entry in .warren/triggers.yaml is now commented out by deliberate operator decision, and the
four Audit Warden agents are retired. bugwatch still ships as a built-in but is unscheduled
here, so its 1/6 sample is frozen and not worth chasing on its own.

This seed is now the PREREQ for re-enabling the single nightwatch example trigger. Scope
narrows to nightwatch's two dominant failure modes:
  - never_started (4 runs) — pod never started; suspect cluster capacity/quota (warren-cca7).
  - dropped_commit (1 run) — distinguish 'agent forgot to commit' from 'agent was killed
    mid-commit'; the fixes differ.
  - crashed (3 runs) — still needs event-log triage.
Do not re-enable the weekly nightwatch block in .warren/triggers.yaml until never_started is
either fixed or surfaced as an explicit operator-visible condition rather than a silent
failed run.

title: deploy-gke: pushes to main build images but never roll GKE, so prod silently lags main by days
description:
warren-1f12 (blank /#/runs/:id) merged to main 2026-07-23 in #626-#628 but did not reach production until 2026-07-25 16:45Z, when someone manually ran a workflow_dispatch with deploy:true. Root cause: .github/workflows/deploy-gke.yml gates its deploy job on `github.event_name == 'release' || (workflow_dispatch && inputs.deploy) || (push && ref == refs/heads/k8s-migration)`. A bare push to main builds + pushes images and stops. The k8s-migration branch merged in v0.10.0 (see abed4b0 'defaultBranch k8s-migration -> main'), so the one branch that auto-deployed no longer exists — leaving NO automatic deploy path between releases.

Consequences: (1) 'main is green' does not mean 'prod is green'; a breaking change can sit undeployed for days and then land all at once on an unrelated manual dispatch, which is exactly how the blank-page incident presented as 'this just happened'. (2) The version string compounds it — package.json has not been bumped since the v0.10.1 tag (2026-07-21), so the live app self-reports 0.10.1 while running ~20 commits of main, making it look like the tagged release introduced the bug.

Decide and implement one of: (a) auto-deploy on push to main (continuous deployment, matches the dogfood posture the k8s-migration branch had); (b) keep release-gated deploys but make the lag VISIBLE — surface deployed SHA vs main HEAD in /readyz or the UI footer; (c) cut releases often enough that the release trigger is the deploy path in practice. Also fix the stale k8s-migration branch condition either way, and consider serving the deployed git SHA (not just VERSION) from metaApi.version so 'what is actually running' is answerable without reading workflow logs.
closeReason: Fixed by warren-8b5f (commit be5417f6, 2026-07-27): deploy-gke.yml rewritten — release.yml invokes deploy-gke via workflow_call with deploy:true plus a post-deploy /version smoke test; stale push/branch trigger removed

title: Stop forwarding raw Error.message on unhandled 500s (src/server/errors.ts:85-90)
description:
Step 1 of pl-b82d (phase 0 — security). Prerequisite for the response-projection work in steps 14-16: as long as any handler can emit a raw Error.message, projecting the happy path is pointless.

PROBLEM
`src/server/errors.ts:85-90` forwards `error.message` verbatim on any unhandled 500. Subprocess stderr, filesystem paths, and driver strings escape from EVERY route, including ones that will be anonymous. `src/server/handlers/projects.ts:100-102` already concedes in-comment that `SeedsCliError` bubbles out this way.

SCOPE
- `src/server/errors.ts` — split the response body from the log record. Known/typed application errors (ValidationError, NotFoundError, ProjectLacksSeedsError, and friends) keep their message; anything else returns a generic message plus a correlation id.
- Emit the full error (message + stack) to the pino logger at error level with that same correlation id, so operators lose nothing. `src/server/main/redact.ts` already covers the log side.
- Audit every `throw` reachable from a handler for typed-vs-untyped classification; grep `src/server/handlers/` for raw `throw new Error(`.
- Update `src/server/__golden__/responses/*` fixtures whose bodies change, and `responses.golden.test.ts`.

ACCEPTANCE
- A handler throwing an untyped Error returns a body containing no filesystem path, no subprocess output, and no driver text — only a generic message and a correlation id.
- The same request logs the full message and stack, findable by correlation id.
- Typed application errors are unchanged in body and status.
- New test asserts an untyped throw does not leak `process.cwd()` or a `/data/` path into the response.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Remove secret-adjacent disclosure from /readyz and /metrics diagnostics payloads
description:
Step 2 of pl-b82d (phase 0 — security). A live disclosure on the current deployment, independent of any public demo.

PROBLEM
- `src/diagnostics/checks-preview.ts:151` publishes **`WARREN_API_TOKEN.length`** in the `/readyz` payload. Token length is a real search-space reduction and there is no reason to expose it.
- `src/diagnostics/checks-config.ts:269-279` surfaces raw DB driver errors including host, port and user.
- The payload also carries server filesystem paths and project ids.

SCOPE
- `src/diagnostics/checks-preview.ts` — replace the length disclosure with a boolean `configured: true|false`.
- `src/diagnostics/checks-config.ts` — classify driver errors into a fixed set of reasons (`unreachable`, `auth_failed`, `migration_pending`, `unknown`); log the raw text, never return it.
- Sweep the rest of `src/diagnostics/` for absolute paths in check details; return basenames or a boolean.
- `src/server/handlers/diagnostics.ts` and `src/server/handlers/metrics.ts` stay auth-gated — do NOT add them to `isAuthExempt` (`src/server/handlers/index.ts:330-347`). Step 13 will hard-block both for anonymous callers; this step reduces the blast radius for an operator-token holder and for anyone who later relaxes the gate.
- Update golden fixtures under `src/server/__golden__/responses/`.

ACCEPTANCE
- `/readyz` contains no token length, no DB host/port/user, and no absolute filesystem path.
- Operator diagnostic value is preserved: each degraded check still names what is wrong via a stable reason code.
- Test asserts the `/readyz` body does not match `/[0-9]{2,}/` for the token check and contains no `/data/` substring.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Stop embedding the bearer token in preview-login URLs (client.ts buildPreviewLoginUrl, RunDetail href)
description:
Step 3 of pl-b82d (phase 0 — security).

PROBLEM
`src/ui/src/api/client.ts:288-292` (`buildPreviewLoginUrl`) embeds the raw bearer token in a URL query string. It is rendered as a clickable `<a href>` at `src/ui/src/pages/RunDetail.tsx:409` and `:435-445`. Tokens in URLs land in browser history, `Referer` headers, and any proxy or analytics log in the path. On a public instance this must never render at all; on the private instance it is already a leak.

SCOPE
- Replace the query-string handshake with a POST that sets the preview session cookie server-side, or a short-lived single-use handoff token minted by the server and distinct from `WARREN_API_TOKEN`.
- Server side lives behind the preview-login exemption regex in `src/server/handlers/index.ts:330-347` — keep the exemption narrow and update it to match the new shape.
- `src/ui/src/pages/RunDetail.tsx:409,435-445` — the affordance becomes a button, not an href.
- Check `src/preview/` for any other place the token is threaded into a URL.

ACCEPTANCE
- No code path places `WARREN_API_TOKEN` (or any bearer) into a URL, query string, or `href`.
- Preview login still works end to end against a live preview.
- Test asserts `buildPreviewLoginUrl` (or its replacement) returns a URL whose query string contains no token-shaped value.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Cap concurrent event-stream connections on GET /runs/:id/events (idleTimeout:0 + single replica DoS)
description:
Step 4 of pl-b82d (phase 0 — security/availability).

PROBLEM
`src/server/server.ts:55` sets `idleTimeout: 0` server-wide so long-lived NDJSON event streams survive quiet stretches. Combined with a single-replica control plane (`deploy/k8s/base/deployment.yaml:18-23`, `strategy: Recreate`, no horizontal scaling available because of SSE stickiness and an RWO PVC) and no connection cap anywhere, `GET /runs/:id/events?follow=1` is an unbounded connection-exhaustion vector. A Show HN spike hits this even without malice.

SCOPE
- Add a global and per-IP concurrent-stream cap enforced where streams are established — `src/server/handlers/runs/events.ts:25` and the plan-run twin at `src/server/handlers/plan-runs.ts:316`. Over the cap returns 503 with `Retry-After`, not a hang.
- Make the caps env-tunable with sane defaults (suggest global 200, per-IP 5) and document them in `.env.example`.
- `src/runs/events.ts` `RunEventBroker.subscriberCount(runId)` already exists — reuse it rather than adding a parallel counter where possible.
- Consider a per-connection max lifetime so a wedged client cannot hold a slot forever.
- Emit a metric for current stream count so `/metrics` shows saturation.

ACCEPTANCE
- Exceeding the per-IP cap returns 503 + `Retry-After`; existing streams are unaffected.
- Exceeding the global cap does the same and logs at warn.
- Caps are configurable via env with documented defaults.
- Test opens N+1 streams and asserts the last is rejected and the first N still deliver events.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Add scripts/version-bump.ts porting burrow's, extended to README status line, openapi regen, and a drafted [Unreleased] section
description:
Step 5 of pl-b82d (phase B1 — release machinery).

CONTEXT
CLAUDE.md:290-291 and `.claude/commands/release.md:14` both state there is no `version:bump` script here. Burrow has one — `/Users/jayminwest/Projects/os-eco/burrow/scripts/version-bump.ts`, 62 lines, atomic two-file rewrite with rollback on failure at `:50`. Port it and extend.

SCOPE
- New `scripts/version-bump.ts` + `"version:bump"` in package.json. Accepts `major|minor|patch|<explicit>`.
- Rewrites, atomically: `package.json` `version`, `src/index.ts` `export const VERSION`.
- Runs `bun run gen:openapi` so `docs/openapi.yaml:6` (auto-derived from package.json by `scripts/generate-openapi.ts:169-173`) stays synced.
- Rewrites the README status line — currently `README.md:38` reads `Stable (0.9.10)` against an actual 0.10.1.
- Drafts a `[Unreleased]` section into CHANGELOG.md from `git log <last-tag>..HEAD` PR titles, clearly marked as a draft for a human to edit down. **Assistive only — this is not enforcement.** Per the plan's alternatives, CHANGELOG curation stays human and there is no per-PR CI gate.
- Prints exact next steps (commit, push, what will fire).
- Co-located test, following burrow's.
- Delete the "there is no version:bump" claims from CLAUDE.md:290-291 and `.claude/commands/release.md:14`.

ACCEPTANCE
- `bun run version:bump patch` updates all four version sites and leaves a draft CHANGELOG section.
- A failure partway through rolls back cleanly (burrow's `:50` pattern).
- No CI or PR gate is added by this step.
- `bun run check:all` green.

title: Add check:version-sync gate covering package.json, src/index.ts, docs/openapi.yaml and the README status line
description:
Step 6 of pl-b82d (phase B1). Blocked on step 5 (warren-16b5).

PROBLEM
Version lives in five places. `release.yml:46-54` verifies only `package.json` vs `src/index.ts` — and only at release time, on the release branch. README has drifted two releases (`README.md:38` says 0.9.10, actual 0.10.1) and `docs/openapi.yaml` drift is invisible because CI does not run `gen:openapi:check` (step 7 fixes that half).

SCOPE
- New `scripts/check-version-sync.ts` asserting agreement across: `package.json` `version`, `src/index.ts` `VERSION`, `docs/openapi.yaml` `info.version`, and the README status line.
- Also assert the burrow-cli pin agrees between `README.md:75` and `Dockerfile:93` — they currently disagree (0.3.12 vs 0.3.15). Same class of drift, same script.
- Register in the `GATES` manifest in `scripts/check-all.ts` and add the script to package.json. Note `scripts/check-all.ts` is byte-identical to `templates/l5-toolkit/scripts/check-all.ts` and must NOT be edited — per CLAUDE.md all per-repo variation comes from package.json, filtered against the frozen canonical gate order. If the canonical order has no slot for this gate, fold the assertions into an existing gate rather than editing the frozen script.
- Note `release.yml:46-54` uses GNU-only `grep -oP`; the new script should not depend on that.

ACCEPTANCE
- Bumping package.json alone fails `bun run check:all` with a message naming every out-of-sync file.
- The gate passes on a clean tree today only after the README and burrow-cli pins are corrected (do that in this step).
- `scripts/check-all.ts` and `scripts/check-ci-parity.ts` remain byte-identical to the l5-toolkit copies.
